evidence_excerpts: The bzip2 case study reports that training on the combined input results in performance gains of about 8%, training on xml improves performance by only 2%, and best-case FDO performance for individual inputs has a minimum improvement of about 4% and a maximum gain of about 13%.
text: For bzip2 on Itanium, the training input materially changes inlining performance, with combined training giving about an 8 percent gain, xml training about a 2 percent gain, and best-case per-input FDO gains ranging roughly from 4 to 13 percent.
